text: . Director General, Akashvani, Rajeev Kumar Jain, today chaired a review meeting of Regional Channel Managers of the North Zone at Akashvani Srinagar. The meeting is being held to discuss sales and content of Akashvani Regional Channels in the North Zone, besides reviewing their overall performance and functioning.Speaking on the occasion, DG Akashvani Rajeev Jain urged the RCMs to make full use of the powers and flexibility provided under the decentralised framework introduced last year. The DG said the meeting was aimed at understanding the issues faced by RCMs, seeking their feedback and finding solutions to their requirements of RCMs across the country. Mr Jain said the performance of RCMs is reviewed regularly and stressed that both public service and commercial responsibilities have to be taken together. He said the deliberations are important for further strengthening the content and sales performance of Akashvani stations across the country.

. National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Managing Director and CEO Dilip Asbe today said around 75 per cent of transaction volumes would fall outside the scope of the new merchant discount rate (MDR) regime, as 96 per cent of transactions are below 2,000 rupees.Addressing the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai, Asbe said there is “huge miscommunication and misinformation” surrounding the MDR regime and that NPCI and the government is trying to provide clear information.Mr Asbe clarified that the new regime will not hurt UPI volumes because most of the MDR will come from merchants who already accept credit cards and therefore, already pay MDR.

. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won a bronze in the men’s double sculls as India concluded their rowing campaign at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with one medal today. The Indian pair clocked 6:13.25 at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course to finish behind China’s Yi Xudi and Nie Yide, who won gold in 6:09.77.Uzbekistan’s Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov and Pavel Sorin took silver in 6:10.49. It was India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in the men’s double sculls. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has lauded the Indian duo after their bronze-winning feat at the games

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for stronger international cooperation on peace, democracy, development and regional cooperation while addressing the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.Reaffirming Bangladesh’s commitment to multilateralism, disarmament and peaceful resolution of conflicts, PM Rahman said international disputes should be addressed through dialogue, diplomacy and mutual cooperation. He also reiterated Bangladesh’s support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and to establish an independent State of Palestine.On the Rohingya crisis, the PM called for stronger international support for the safe and sustainable repatriation of more than 1.2 million Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh. He urged the United Nations and the international community to continue life-saving humanitarian assistance until their repatriation to Myanmar.Addressing climate change, PM Rahman called for greater climate finance, adaptation support and climate justice. He highlighted Bangladesh’s programmes for tree plantation, clean and solar energy, water conservation, and excavation of canals.The Prime Minister outlined his government’s three-R strategy-Recovery, Restoration and Reconstruction-for rebuilding Bangladesh. He highlighted initiatives focused on employment generation, entrepreneurship, women’s empowerment, education, healthcare and social protection.He also called for equitable access to artificial intelligence and advanced technologies for developing countries, along with technology transfer, skills development and capacity building.Concluding his address, PM Rahman said Bangladesh seeks to build a prosperous, self-reliant and welfare-oriented democratic society where people can live with equal rights, respect and dignity.

. In the Asian Games, the Indian duo Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh stormed into the final of the mixed team 10m air pistol event after topping the qualification with a strong performance today in Nagoya, Japan.After registering a 196 in the opening series, the Indian pair raced to 391 at the end of second series after scoring 195, placing them within sight of making the finals with just 20 shots remaining. They aggregated another 196 in the third series to take their tally to 587, which included 29 inner 10s. The top four pairs advance to the final. This is India’s final chance for a medal in the 10m air pistol events after a disappointing campaign so far.In table tennis mixed doubles, India’s Manush Shah and Diya Chitale stunned world No. 4 Doo Hoi Kem and Wong Chun Ting of Hong Kong 3-1 to reach the semi finals at the Asian Games. The Indian duo won 11-6, 13-15, 11-9, 11-5 in the quarterfinals to secure India’s first table tennis medal at the ongoing Games. Shah and Chitale will now face China’s Sun Yingsha and Wang Chuqin in the semifinals.

. Bangladesh has suspended hilsa imports from India. The decision took effect yesterday, halting hilsa imports through the Benapole land port. Bangladesh importers have expressed concern over financial losses following the sudden suspension.The decision is currently affecting the import channel through Benapole, where Indian hilsa had been entering Bangladesh under the approved import arrangements.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Indian shooters Kamaljeet and Suruchi Inder Singh for clinching Gold Medal in the 10-meter Air Pistol Mixed Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that it was a fine display of precision and partnership.Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya has also congratulated the shooters for clinching the Gold Medal.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that Viksit Bharat can be realised only with the contribution and participation of everyone. Mr Modi made these remarks during a virtual interaction with Seva Yatris travelling on the Yatra from Varanasi to Vadnagar under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. Mr Modi highlighted that Vadnagar gave him the values that shaped his life, while Kashi added countless colours of service to those values. He expressed happiness that young people are also enriching this journey with the many colours of service.The Prime Minister noted that over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has narrowed significantly. Today, infrastructure in villages has improved considerably, while self-reliance among the women of the country has also increased.Mr Modi said that today marks the birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya. He highlighted the seven principles given by Pandit Upadhyaya of service, balance, patience, coordination, positivity, sensitivity and dialogue. He added that every BJP worker takes pride in following the path shown by Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya with a spirit of service.During the interaction these yatris shared their experiences with the Prime Minister. Mr Modi also urged the yatris to maintain a diary and record their experiences during the Yatra.

. Foreign Ministers of the G4 countries-India, Brazil, Germany and Japan- have called for early reform of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC). In a joint ministerial statement, they emphasised that expansion of the Council in both permanent and non-permanent categories is central to the reform. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar, Foreign Minister of Brazil Mauro Vieira, Foreign Affairs Minister of Germany Johann David Wadephul and Foreign Affairs Minister of Japan Motegi Toshimitsu held the meeting on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.The Ministers said that UNSC reform is more necessary than ever before, given the increasingly challenging geopolitical environment. They also underlined the need for greater representation of under-represented and unrepresented regions and groups, including Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America and the Caribbean. The G4 Ministers noted that the UNSC is currently unable to effectively discharge its core responsibility of maintaining international peace and security. They said the representativeness, legitimacy, credibility and efficacy of the Council are in question.They also reviewed discussions on UNSC reform under the Inter-governmental Negotiations framework during the 80th session of the UN General Assembly and discussed the overall state of play regarding the prospects of reform.The G4 Ministers expressed concern over the lack of concrete progress in the Inter-governmental Negotiations framework towards UNSC reform. They also expressed reservations over the presentation of a bridging proposal before the commencement of text-based negotiations. They said the G4 will further collaborate with other reform-oriented groups to develop a consolidated model reflecting the views of a majority of UN Member States and to commence text-based negotiations as a high priority.

. In the Asian Games, 2026 Indian runners have clinched silver in the mixed 4x400m relay race at Nagoya today. The quartet of Poovamma Raju, Vishal Thennarasu, Vithya Ramraj and Manu TS timed the run at 3 mins 14.46 seconds to defend India’s silver medal won in the last edition of the games in Hangzhou. Bahrain won the gold with Games record of 3 mins 12.87 seconds.Before that, Seema Kumari won bronze in the 10,000 metre race after finishing at third spot in 32.50 mins. The achievement marks India’s first medal in the women’s 10,000m event at the Asian Games in 16 years.Earlier, in Shooting, Anant Jeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal also bagged bronze in the mixed skeet team event, the first-ever medal for India in this category. The Indian pair missed just four of 48 shots and finished level with South Korea, but lost to South Korea in the tie-breaker. China won Gold.In Boxing, Parveen made it to the quarterfinals of the Women’s 65kg category after receiving a walkover from Tajikistan’s Malika Nozimova in the round of 16 at Nishio. She will now face reigning world silver medallist Navbakhor Khamidova of Uzbekistan.In the morning, Indian wushu player Roshibina Devi Naorem won Silver in the Women’s 60kg Sanda event after losing 0-2 to China’s Zhang Xiaoyu in the final. It was third Asian Games medal for Roshibina, after Silver 2023 Hangzhou Games and Bronze in 2018 Jakarta-Palembang Games. In Men’s double sculls rowing, Satnam Singh and Salman Khan won bronze.However, Commonwealth Games champion Sakshi Chaudhary bowed out of the Games after her loss in the Women’s 51 kg pre-quarters to reigning World Champion Alua Balkibekova.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated medal winning players.

. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed a nationwide ban on the manufacture and sale of the analogue product as paneer. In a notification, the FSSAI stated that the products already licensed or registered under the ‘Analogue in Dairy Context’ category shall discontinue the use of the term ‘Paneer’ in their nomenclature, labelling, or marketing.The FSSAI has proposed an amendment to the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, for Analogue Paneer. This has been done to restrict the manufacturing and sale of analogue products so that consumers are not misled regarding the nature and composition of the product.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Pune will host the UCI Road World Championships in 2032, marking the first time cycling’s prestigious global road championships to be held in India. The decision was announced at the UCI Congress in Montreal, following Pune’s final candidature presentation.The bid was jointly led by the Government of Maharashtra and the Cycling Federation of India, with support from the Government of India. Pune’s candidature reached the final round against Groningen/Drenthe of the Netherlands, after Colombia and Mexico were eliminated. A UCI inspection team had earlier assessed proposed venues, including Balewadi Stadium and the Pune University circuit.The championships will bring the world’s leading road cyclists to India to compete for the coveted rainbow jerseys. Cycling Federation of India Secretary General Maninder Pal Singh said the event will help strengthen pathways for Indian athletes, coaches and technical officials and provide greater international exposure for the country’s cycling community.

. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has issued an advisory to the common public about ‘Nidhi Companies’ and their functioning. The Ministry has warned against investment decisions without a proper background check, especially if there is a promise of high returns.The Nidhi companies are mutual-benefit companies regulated by the Corporate Affairs Ministry under the Companies Act, 2013 and Nidhi Rules, 2014, which can accept deposits and give loans only to their members.The Ministry said that during examination of NDH-4 applications, it was noticed that many ‘Nidhi’ Companies are not complying with the applicable provisions of the Act and rules made there under in toto.The Ministry informed that the deposits accepted by Nidhi Companies are not insured by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation.  It added that if the company fails or faces fraud, recovery of deposited money can be very difficult or incomplete.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices slumped over 1.6 percent today. The Sensex tanked 1, 248 points to close at 73, 581 while the Nifty plunged 384 points to settle at 23,063.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index shed 2.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index lost over 1.5%.This morning, Markets opened with a gap-down as spike in bond yields, elevated crude oil prices and a sell-off in banking and insurance stocks weighed on the indices. The Sensex and Nifty remained under pressure throughout the session, with sell-off intensifying during the second half of the trade.In the Sensex pack, 29 out of 30 companies logged losses with NTPC remaining unchanged. Among the top under performers, Bajaj Finance lost 5.5%, Axis Bank declined 4.7 per cent and Bajaj Finserv fell 4.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top losers, Mid-Small Private Banks declined 2.8 per cent, Housing Finance lost 2.6 per cent and Financial Services shed more than 2.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,884 companies declined, 1,473 advanced and 216 remained unchanged.

. Defending champions India held Azerbaijan to a 2-2 draw in the eighth round of the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand yesterday. R Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi, D Gukesh and Vidit Santosh Gujrathi were all held to draws by their Azerbaijani opponents.Gukesh drew with Muradli Mahammad after 56 moves, while Praggnanandhaa drew with Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, Arjun with Aydin Suleymanli and Vidit with Rauf Mamedov. India remained in joint second place in the Open section with 13 match points. Uzbekistan and Germany share the lead with 14 match points after Germany defeated the hosts 2.5-1.5.In the women’s section, defending champions India drew 2-2 with Kazakhstan and remained in joint second place. B Savitha Shri secured her seventh consecutive victory by defeating Elnaz Kaliakhmet. Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh drew, while Vaishali Rameshbabu lost to Nurman Alua..

. Today marks 12 years of Make in India. It was on this day in 2014 that the initiative was launched with the ambition of becoming a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. The initiative has transformed India’s manufacturing landscape by expanding production, investment and capabilities across industries.Akashvani correspondent reports that over the years, Make in India has opened new opportunities for businesses and investors to participate in India’s manufacturing journey. The initiative has subsequently been expanded under Make in India 2.0. The initiative now focuses on 27 sectors, which include 15 in manufacturing and 12 in services.The initiative focused on facilitating investment, fostering innovation and developing world-class infrastructure. Guided by ‘Minimum Government, Maximum Governance’, it has also sought to modernise processes and policies. Under the initiative, India’s electronics production increased nearly sevenfold, from 1.9 lakh crore rupees in 2014-15 to over 13 lakh crore in 2025-26. Mobile-phone production rose approximately 33-fold, from 18 thousand crore to 6.27 lakh crore over the same period.During this period, Indian Railways manufactured nearly 55 thousand coaches over 2014-24, while average annual railway coach production rose from less than 3 thousand 300 during 2004-14 to over 5 thousand during 2014-24. Over 6 thousand 6 hundred Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches were manufactured in 2025-26.Further, under the Make in India initiative, the country’s indigenous defence production increased from 46 thousand 429 crore in 2014-15 to a record 1.78 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26, bringing production to nearly four times its 2014-15 level. The initiative now goes beyond producing more goods and focuses on building the skills, technology and capacity needed to make them in India.

. In Shooting, Anant Jeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal bagged the bronze medal in the mixed skeet team event at Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan today. The medal is India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in the mixed skeet team category. The Indian pair missed just four of their 48 shots and finished level with South Korea, but lost in the tie-break. They finished just one point behind the leading Chinese pair to secure India another shooting medal. China defeated South Korea by 52-51 to win Gold.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the Men’s Badminton Team on winning the Bronze Medal at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that the medal reflects their passion and hard work. Mr Modi said that the entire team displayed great spirit throughout the competition and wished them for the events ahead.The Prime Minister also congratulated Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Anantjeet Singh Naruka on winning the Bronze Medal in the Skeet Mixed Team event. Mr Modi said that their achievement marks India’s first-ever medal in this event at the Asian Games. Wishing the players, he said that their success inspires many more milestones in the times to come.Mr Modi also congratulated Seema on winning the Bronze Medal in the Women’s 10,000m at the Asian Games. He said that her determined performance has brought India a medal in this event after many years. The Prime Minister described it as a wonderful achievement that reflects endurance, discipline and years of hard work and wished her many more successes in the times ahead.

. India won a silver medal in the mixed 4x400m relay at the Asian Games in Nagoya today. The quartet of Poovamma Raju, Vishal Thennarasu, Vithya Ramraj and Manu TS claimed the silver medal with a timing of 3:14.46, successfully defending the medal they won in the last edition in 2023 in Hangzhou. Bahrain won the gold with Games record of 3:12.87.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today. The Sensex rose 299 points or 0.4 per cent to close at 74,828. The Nifty jumped 118 points or half a per cent to settle at 23,447.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index climbed 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today held a discussion with the European Parliament delegation focusing on effective implementation of India-EU FTA. The delegation,comprisingmembers of the European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy, met Dr Singh in New Delhi. During the meeting, both sides discussed deepening cooperation in Science, Technology and Emerging Technologies.On the occasion, Dr Singh said the India-EU strategic partnership offers significant opportunities for closer collaboration in areas of mutual priority, with science and research forming an integral part of the partnership. He added that the FTA will open new opportunities for businesses, consumers and skilled professionals and provide further momentum to the multifaceted India-EU strategic partnership.Member of European Parliament Angelika Winzig said that India is a key strategic partner for the European Union. She said the delegation’s visit was aimed at gaining a deeper understanding of India’s industrial and technology policies and identifying areas for closer cooperation.

. Bangladesh’s national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines, has signed an agreement with Boeing to purchase 11 new aircraft, thereby planning to expand its aviation sector and open new international routes.Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Adviser Mahdi Amin, addressing a press conference in New York said the agreement was signed in the presence of senior US officials, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau.Mr. Amin said the purchase was based on Bangladesh’s expanding aviation needs and plans to introduce new routes. He added that Bangladesh has a longstanding commercial relationship with Boeing and may also hold discussions with Airbus in the future. The adviser said a Boeing delegation later met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

. Seema Kumari has bagged a bronze medal for India in the women’s 10,000 metre final at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi Nagoya in Japan. She crossed the finish line with a time of 32:50.05 to secure a bronze medal this evening. This achievement marks India’s first medal in the women’s 10,000m event at the Asian Games in 16 years.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Rohit Jain today said technology was no longer merely an enabler of banking but was increasingly becoming part of banks’ risk architecture.Addressing the 13th SBI Banking & Economics Conclave 2026 in Mumbai, Mr Jain highlighted the growing role of technology in banking and said technology is now embedded in almost every critical banking function, from core banking and payments to customer onboarding, credit assessment, fraud monitoring, and even regulatory reporting.On artificial intelligence, Jain said it could improve customer service, fraud detection, risk assessment and productivity, but could also amplify errors and influence decisions related to credit, fraud alerts, customer access, pricing and service delivery.Mr Jain that boards and senior management must have sufficient technological understanding to question assumptions, assess dependencies and ensure that resilience arrangements are properly tested.

. Secretary (West) Sibi George participated in the second G7 Development Ministers meeting organised by the G7 Chair, France, on the sidelines of the UNGA in New York.In his remarks, Mr George emphasized India’s human-centric and inclusive path of development, anchored in the principles of ‘Sarvodaya’. Citing India’s development partnership initiatives, Secretary (West) emphasized India’s position that development is not merely the provision of financing but about building domestic capabilities and strengthening resilience.Earlier, Mr George also participated in a High-Level Side co-hosted by Ghana, Germany and France  Reparatory Justice. He highlighted the need for stronger international cooperation to facilitate the return and restitution of cultural properties and heritage to their countries and communities of origin.

. The fourth edition of the UP International Trade Show (UPITS) will begin today at the India Expo Centre and Mart in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate the five-day event. The exhibition, themed ‘Ultimate Sourcing Begins Here’, will run until September 29th, connecting the state’s entrepreneurs, manufacturers and exporters directly with the global market.Briefing the media, Uttar Pradesh MSME Minister Bhupendra Chaudhary highlighted the objective of establishing Uttar Pradesh as a global sourcing hub. He said the state is home to over 96 lakh MSME units and stated that UPITS will provide them with new opportunities for market expansion, investment, exports and employment. Akashvani correspondent reports that the event is expected to witness participation of over 2,400 exhibitors, 1.5 lakh B2B buyers and more than 4.5 lakh general visitors.Over 550 international buyers from 85 countries are also expected to attend the event. Partner countries for this edition include Austria, Japan, Russia, Singapore, Belarus and Vietnam. Additionally, reflecting the prominent role of women in trade and industry, around 300 women representatives will actively participate in the event. The exhibition will showcase various industries and sectors, including agriculture, automobiles, defence, IT, health, tourism and renewable energy. A major highlight this year is the introduction of the ‘One District, One Cuisine’ initiative, which will be featured alongside the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme to present the state’s traditional culinary heritage to the world. Buyers and exhibitors can pre-schedule their B2B meetings through a dedicated UPITS app. The event will also feature knowledge sessions, fashion shows and cultural programmes.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said its special US dollar-Indian rupee (USD-INR) forex swap facility has received forex inflows of over 143.5 billion US dollars till September 18, 2026. According to the latest data, Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] deposits accounted for the overwhelming majority, amounting to 132.98 billion US dollars. Meanwhile, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in 5.32 billion US dollars and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) contributed 5.29 billion US dollars. The Apex Bank introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility covering FCNR(B) deposits, ECBs and OFCBs inflows on June 8, 2026, to boost the inflow of dollars amid a weakening rupee. The FCNR(B) deposits scheme was closed on August 31, 2026, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs remains available until December 31, 2026

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Bangladesh has reported 1,782 new dengue cases and eight deaths in the past 24 hours, taking the total number of dengue deaths this year to 209 and cases to 69,149, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Dhaka and Khulna divisions reported the highest numbers of new dengue cases, with 371 and 286 patients respectively.Meanwhile, five more children have died with suspected measles in the past 24 hours, taking the combined deaths from confirmed and suspected measles cases to 1,081 since March 15.Bangladesh DGHS ALSO reported 1,183 new suspected measles cases and 100 confirmed cases during the same period. Since March 15, Bangladesh has recorded 20,951 confirmed cases and 184,632 suspected cases. A total of 101 children have died from confirmed measles, while 980 deaths have been attributed to suspected measles.

. Defending champions India have stormed into the men’s kabaddi semi-finals with a convincing 37-21 victory over Chinese Taipei in their final Group A fixture. India dominated from the outset, taking a commanding 23-11 lead at half-time and maintaining their advantage in the second half, which they won 14-10.The victory was India’s fourth consecutive win in the group stage. India had earlier defeated South Korea, Japan and Bangladesh to finish the group stage unbeaten and secure at least a bronze medal. India scored 28 points through successful raids, three bonus points and six points from all-outs in the match. Kabaddi has been a part of the Asian Games since 1990, and the Indian men’s team has won nine medals, including eight golds.Meanwhile, the Indian women’s team also continued its winning campaign, defeating Iran 37-23 after beating Bangladesh in its opening match. The women’s team will next face hosts Japan in their Group A fixture.

. The Government today clarified that GST on UPI Merchant Discount Rate, or MDR, will not burden small merchants or make digital payments expensive. In a social media post, National Payments Corporation of India  (NPCI) has termed such media reports as incorrect. It said, MDR applies only to person-to-merchant transactions above two thousand rupees. It said person-to-merchant transactions up to two thousand rupees continue to have zero MDR and therefore zero GST impact. NPCI stated that transactions of up to two thousand rupees constitute more than 96 per cent of UPI merchant transaction volume. The GST paid on MDR by a merchant will be adjusted against the GST payable on the sale of goods, in the same manner that input taxes are set off against output tax liability. NPCI said that merchants with monthly UPI receipts of up to one lakh rupees are not liable to pay MDR.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a major overhaul of the insurance distribution framework, including a simpler three-tier architecture, lower expense limits, revamped commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.The insurance regulator released a public consultation paper on “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”, outlining reforms covering distribution structure, expenses, commissions, market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure.Under the proposed norms, insurers and large distribution entities will have to disclose their commission policies and structures in a simple and accessible manner. Specified commercial policies will also carry commission disclosures, enabling customers to be aware of the distribution costs built into the pricing. The consultation paper also proposes tighter measures to curb mis-selling and compulsory bundling of insurance with other financial products.These include documenting customer needs and suitability, bringing direct and indirect remuneration within the regulatory definition of commission, and prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and Non-Banking Financial Company staff selling insurance. IRDAI has further proposed linking the identity of the individual seller with each policy, placing information on mis-selling incidents in the public domain and allowing commission claw-backs in cases of mis-selling.A key part of the proposed reforms is a reduction in insurers’ Expense of Management (EoM) limits. For life insurers, the EoM limit would shift to a company-level basis linked to Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI), with the ceiling proposed at 15 per cent within two years and 12.5 per cent within five years. For general insurers, the calculation would shift from Gross Written Premium (GWP) to domestic GDPI, while the EoM limit would progressively decline from 30 per cent of GWP to 20 per cent of GDPI within five years.

External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar chaired a meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation, FIPIC, on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York yesterday. The meeting reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthen the FIPIC partnership and cooperation in regional and multilateral fora. It was the second Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held under the FIPIC framework.During the meeting, the participating leaders reviewed the outcomes of the FIPIC Summits and welcomed the progress in India-Pacific Islands Countries cooperation, including under the 12-Point Action Plan announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2023. They also discussed further cooperation in renewable energy, climate action, disaster resilience, education, healthcare and capacity building.The meeting was attended by the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance of Samoa; Foreign Ministers of Fiji, Marshall Islands, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Tuvalu; and the Finance Minister of Tonga. The Secretary of the Department of Justice and Attorney General of the Federated States of Micronesia; the Health Minister of Vanuatu; the Deputy Foreign Minister of Naoero; and the Secretary-General of the Pacific Islands Forum also attended the meeting.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today absorbed 75,026 crore rupees from the banking system through an overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction, amid surplus liquidity. The RBI absorbed the liquidity at a cut-off and weighted average rate of 5.24 per cent.According to RBI data, as on 22nd September, liquidity in the banking system was in surplus of 4.45 trillion rupees. The RBI has been conducting VRRR auctions to absorb excess liquidity and align overnight money market rates with the repo rate. The central bank has also conducted open market operations (OMO) sales of government securities worth 50,000 crore rupees on 17th September and 25,000 crore rupees on 21st September.The remaining 25,000 crore rupees tranche is scheduled for 28th September. The RBI had announced total OMO sales of one trillion rupees in three tranches to manage liquidity conditions.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. India will host the prestigious UCI Road World Championships for the first time in 2032, with Pune selected as the host city. The decision is being seen as a significant milestone for the sporting ambitions of Maharashtra as well as the country.The decision was announced at the UCI Congress held in Montreal, Canada, following the final presentation of Pune’s bid. Senior officials of the Maharashtra Government were present in Montreal in support of Pune’s candidature.Hosting the world championship is expected to place Pune prominently on the international cycling map. The event will bring leading cyclists from across the world to the city and is expected to provide a major boost to cycling in Maharashtra and India.The championship is also likely to create opportunities for strengthening cycling infrastructure, training facilities and the overall capacity to host international sporting events. It could further contribute to sports tourism and enhance Pune’s profile as an international sporting destination.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has paid tribute to Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya on his birth anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Modi highlighted that Pandit Upadhyaya regarded the upliftment of the person standing in the last row of society as the foundation of nation-building.The Prime Minister stated that his philosophy of Antyodaya continues to serve as a profound inspiration for public welfare and national progress. On the occasion, Mr Modi urged everyone to reaffirm their resolve to internalise Pandit Upadhyay’s thoughts and ideals to fulfil their social and national responsibilities.

. The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said that its forces had intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis. The coalition said the missiles were aimed at the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said in posts on X that further escalations and violations by the Houthi militia would be dealt with firmly.Saudi Arabia also issued “potential danger” warnings in Makkah and Taif, followed by alerts in Jeddah, Tabuk and Yanbu. Residents were advised to remain indoors or seek shelter. Just a few minutes later, Saudi Civil Defence said the danger had passed in the affected areas.In Yemen, the government forces reportedly repelled overnight Houthi attacks on the Hejat Al-Abd mountain pass, a key supply route to Aden. The route is also important for the movement of goods to Taiz and for residents seeking to travel abroad, as there are no commercial flights from Houthi-controlled areas.The Houthis have continued to put pressure on government forces following their offensive along Yemen’s western coast, which has brought them closer to the Red Sea and the strategic Bab Al-Mandeb strait.

The government has said that 70,000 rural youth across States and Union Territories will be provided skill training from next month under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 2.0. The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme providing placement-linked skill training to poor rural youth. The duration of the training varies from three months to 12 months. The Rural Development Ministry said that all 31 participating States and UTs have been allocated more than nine lakh targets under the scheme for two years period.

. Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal has said that India’s maritime sector is a strong anchor for national progress. In a social media post on World Maritime Day today, Mr Sonowal said, the government is focused on infra modernisation, policy reforms and a resolute Seafarer First vision, which is driving this growth forward.Every year on the final Thursday in September, people around the world commemorate World Maritime Day to recognise the hard work of those who work in the maritime industry. World Maritime Day is being observed today to highlight the importance of the maritime sector and recognise the contribution of seafarers and maritime professionals to global trade and development. The day also draws attention to the vital role of shipping in connecting countries, transporting essential goods and supporting economies across the world.The theme for this year is ‘From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence’. The theme has been selected by the International Maritime Organization, IMO, for 2026 and 2027. It highlights the Organization’s commitment to help Member States put maritime policies and regulations into practice through technical assistance, training and other essential services.The International Maritime Organization, IMO, was established through a Convention adopted on 6th March, 1948. The Convention entered into force on 17th March, 1958, and the Organization held its first meeting in January 1959. IMO develops and maintains a comprehensive international regulatory framework covering maritime safety, security, environmental protection and other aspects of international shipping.International shipping transports more than 80 per cent of global trade to people and communities around the world. World Maritime Day provides an opportunity to recognise the vital role of shipping and to emphasise the importance of implementing international maritime standards effectively.

. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Fatehabad in Agra, Chhote Lal Verma, died yesterday while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Noida. He was reportedly suffering from fever for the past two days.Following a deterioration in his health, the MLA was admitted to a private hospital in Rajpur Chungi, Agra. As his condition did not improve despite treatment, his family members decided to take him to Delhi for further treatment. However, his condition worsened en route, following which he was admitted to a hospital in Noida, where he died during treatment. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath expressed grief over the demise of the Fatehabad MLA.

Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for collective international action on climate change and the Rohingya crisis, outlining five urgent measures in each area during his engagements at the United Nations Headquarters.Addressing a high-level meeting on “Climate Action and the Just Transition”, PM Rahman called for reducing greenhouse gas emissions to keep the 1.5-degree Celsius warming limit under the Paris Agreement, ensuring predictable climate finance for vulnerable countries, expanding access to climate-smart technologies, scaling up renewable energy and fully implementing the Loss and Damage Fund.Highlighting Bangladesh’s climate vulnerability, he said the country contributes less than 0.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions but faces significant climate risks.At a separate high-level side event on the Rohingya crisis, co-convened by Bangladesh and The Gambia, PM Rahman proposed measures including a clear roadmap for safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation of Rohingyas to Myanmar, an end to violence, humanitarian support, stronger accountability and enhanced regional cooperation against transnational crimes.He said more than 1.2 million Rohingyas are sheltered in Bangladesh and stressed that the crisis originated in Myanmar and its solution lies in Myanmar.
